listings.model: Ibanez RG 550 LTD 1994 Made in Japan
listings.title: Ibanez RG 550 LTD 1994 Made in Japan
listings.description:
La Ibanez RG 550 LTD del 1994, Made in Japan, è una delle superstrat che hanno fatto la storia della chitarra rock e metal degli anni '80 e '90: manico Wizard sottile e velocissimo, ponte Lo-Pro Edge e la classica configurazione humbucker-single-humbucker.

Questo esemplare è del 1994, ed è un punto da sottolineare: le RG 550 che si trovano oggi sono quasi tutte riedizioni successive, con differenze di costruzione e di dettaglio rispetto a questa produzione giapponese originale. La chitarra è molto vissuta e lo dichiariamo con chiarezza: la vernice nera presenta numerose scrostature e segni di usura sui bordi, sul retro e nella zona dell'avambraccio, dove in alcuni punti si vede il legno sotto. È usura vera da palco, non trascuratezza: il manico è perfetto e i tasti sono in ottimo stato.

Caratteristiche principali:

  • Anno: 1994, Made in Japan.
  • Finitura: nera, con battipenna perlato.
  • Dettagli costruttivi: manico in acero Wizard, tastiera con intarsi a dente di squalo, paletta classica Ibanez con meccaniche originali.
  • Pickup/Circuito: configurazione HSH (humbucker al ponte e al manico, single coil al centro).
  • Ponte: Ibanez Lo-Pro Edge a doppio bloccaggio.
  • Condizioni: manico perfetto, tasti in ottimo stato; finitura con forte usura e numerose scrostature, legno a vista in alcuni punti (ben visibile nelle foto).
  • Suono: aggressivo e definito, con la versatilità della selezione HSH: dal tagliente del ponte ai suoni puliti e frizzanti delle posizioni intermedie.

Per l'appassionato di RG che cerca una giapponese del 1994 vera, che si suona e non si tiene in vetrina: un esemplare con la sua storia addosso e un manico che non ha perso niente.

The Ibanez RG 550 LTD from 1994, Made in Japan, is one of the superstrats that shaped rock and metal guitar in the '80s and '90s: thin, lightning-fast Wizard neck, Lo-Pro Edge bridge and the classic humbucker-single-humbucker layout.

This one is a 1994, and that matters: most RG 550s around today are later reissues, with construction and detail differences compared to this original Japanese production. The guitar is heavily played and we say so clearly: the black finish shows many chips and wear on the edges, on the back and in the forearm area, where bare wood shows through in places. This is honest stage wear, not neglect: the neck is perfect and the frets are in excellent shape.

Key Features:

  • Year: 1994, Made in Japan.
  • Finish: black, with pearloid pickguard.
  • Build: Wizard maple neck, sharktooth inlays, classic Ibanez headstock with original tuners.
  • Pickups: HSH layout (bridge and neck humbuckers, single coil in the middle).
  • Bridge: Ibanez Lo-Pro Edge double-locking tremolo.
  • Condition: perfect neck, frets in excellent shape; heavy finish wear with many chips, bare wood showing in places (clearly visible in the photos).
  • Iconic Sound: aggressive and articulate, with the versatility of the HSH switching: from the cutting bridge tone to sparkling cleans in the in-between positions.

For the RG enthusiast looking for a genuine 1994 Japanese model to play, not to keep in a display case: a guitar with its history on it and a neck that has lost nothing.

listings.description:
The Ibanez Iron Label RGRB620 offers metal-minded players a satisfying 6-string playing experience. This solidbody electric guitar is built upon an okoume body, carved into Ibanez’s classic RG shape. The RGRB620’s 5-piece maple/walnut neck features a hand-cradling Wizard II shape, and its 24-fret, flat-radius ebony fingerboard provides plenty of room for fast-paced finger maneuverability. A set of DiMarzio D Activator humbuckers delivers a perfect storm of rapid-fire attack and amp-pummeling output, both of which are must-haves for modern metal. The RGRB620 is equipped with an Edge-Zero II double-locking tremolo, putting an entire arsenal of pitch-abusing pyrotechnics at your disposal. Complete with an attention-grabbing reverse headstock and a spotlight-stealing satin poly finish, the Ibanez RGRB620 is the perfect instrument for your individual brand of mind-bending metallurgic musicality.

One of Ibanez’s fastest necks to date, the 5-piece maple/walnut Wizard II neck on the RGRB620 is an absolute pleasure to play. This slim and super-comfortable neck lets you pull off lightning-fast runs, arpeggios, and hammer-ons with ease, but it still gives you the substance you need for fretting chords. Capping the neck is a 24-fret ebony fingerboard that’s loaded with jumbo frets that are perfect for big note bends. From the first time you put your hands on the RGRB620’s Wizard II neck, you’ll know you’ve got a guitar that was built with performance in mind.

Ibanez loaded the Iron Label RGRB620 with a pair of DiMarzio D Activator humbucking pickups. These high-octane pickups deliver a full and enriched harmonic quality that’s great for rhythm and solo playing alike. DiMarzio designed their D Activator pickups to eliminate the sterile edginess that plagues many active pickups. The bottom line is that they deliver all the advantages of active pickups without the drawbacks. Plus, these pickups don’t require batteries! What’s more, their massive headroom permits you to pick as aggressively as you want without flattening your signal. These pickups also have exceptionally balanced volume between the neck and bridge — you can switch between the two positions with zero drops in volume. The RGRB620 includes Ibanez’s vaunted dyna-Mix10 switching system, along with an Alter switch.

Whether you palm mute with precision or simply have a wild strumming style, few things are worse than getting hung up on your bridge during a furious performance. That’s one area in which the RGRB620’s Edge-Zero II tremolo really shines; it gets out of the way of your playing while still serving up maximum expression and tuning stability. You’ll barely know it’s there, thanks to its streamlined profile and recessed fine tuners. Plus, locking studs give you additional tuning stability. As for functionality, we’ve been using — and abusing — Ibanez’s Edge-Zero and its variants around Sweetwater since the early 1990s, and we can proclaim with the utmost confidence: the Edge-Zero II is among the most reliable double-locking trems you’ll ever put your hands on. So, pull the bar all the way up, then slam it down to the body all you want; you can follow it up with a jazz chord, and it’ll be perfectly in tune.

Ibanez Iron Label RGRB620 Features:
  • Offers metal-minded players a satisfying 6-string playing experience
  • Okoume body carved into Ibanez’s classic RG shape
  • 5-piece maple/walnut Wizard II neck provides a just-right feel
  • 24-fret ebony fingerboard with jumbo frets for effortless note bends
  • DiMarzio D Activator humbuckers give you active guitar tones without the battery
  • dyna-Mix10 switching system, along with an Alter switch, unlocks unlimited tonal textures
  • Play expressively while maintaining your tuning stability with the Edge-Zero II tremolo
  • Rock-solid Gotoh tuning machine heads
